plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Exit remaining AI/Software leverage (METU, MUU).
Reduce QQQI concentration to 20%.
Increase broad index exposure with SPY and QQQ.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation.
Expect lower volatility and modest growth.
conservative.read: This mode focuses on preserving capital with minimal drawdown. Expect a target monthly return around 1.5%. Significant risk reduction is achieved by cutting leverage and concentrating on broad market exposure and income.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to minimal levels.
Reduce exposure in AI/Software and Semiconductor leveraged names.
Trim QQQI to reduce concentration.
Add new, high-scoring names like ZS and CRWD.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth opportunities.
Aim for steady, risk-managed growth.
balanced.read: This balanced approach aims for risk-first growth with a target monthly return of approximately 2.5%. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding high-quality, strong-setup names. Drawdowns are expected to be moderate.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL).
Add to AI/Software and Semiconductor leveraged positions.
Trim QQQI to manage concentration.
Initiate new, high-conviction positions like ZS and CRWD.
This plan aggressively pursues growth through leverage and concentration.
Expect higher potential returns but also significantly larger drawdowns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive mode targets substantial growth, aiming for ~4% monthly returns by leaning into leverage and concentration. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and high-scoring setups. Be aware that this strategy carries the highest risk of large drawdowns and amplified losses due to leverage and leveraged ETF decay.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs and volatile single names (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU, SMH).
Increase allocation to income-focused QQQI.
Maintain a significant position in the broad index SPY.
This plan prioritizes steady income generation and capital preservation.
Focus is on monthly distributions rather than aggressive growth.
Expect low volatility and reliable, though variable, income.
income.read: This income-focused mode aims for a target monthly return of around 1% by prioritizing income-generating assets and broad market exposure. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leverage and volatile growth stocks. While aiming for low drawdowns and steady distributions, NAV can still decline in market downturns.
